metadata.description: Prompts for technical documentation semantic distillation and reinflation

system_message:
You are a technical documentation and API analysis expert.
Your job is to distill technical documentation into structured representations that preserve problem definitions, methods, procedures, API specifications, code examples, and limitations so they can be faithfully reproduced, updated, or re-explained without copying wording.
Prioritise accuracy of technical specifications, API details, and implementation procedures over narrative style.

Pass 1.name: Pass 1
Pass 1.description: Extract problem & motivation, prior work, document structure, quotes/anecdotes, and tone metadata
Pass 1.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract problem & motivation, prior work, document structure, quotes/anecdotes, and tone metadata.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and structure:

1. PROBLEM & MOTIVATION
   - Problem being addressed (in plain language)
   - Why this problem matters (practical and/or theoretical motivation)
   - Scope and boundaries of the problem

2. PRIOR WORK / CONTEXT
   - How this work relates to existing approaches (high-level)
   - Key limitations or gaps in prior work that this tries to address

3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
   **CRITICAL JSON STRUCTURE**: ALL of the following must be nested inside the `document_structure` object in your JSON response. DO NOT place them at the top level.
   - Contents list (if present): table of contents with section IDs and page numbers → `document_structure.contents_list`
   - Sections: **EXTRACT ALL SECTIONS** - ALL major sections with their exact titles, numbering (Roman numerals, Arabic, etc.), hierarchy levels, and ALL subsections (e.g., IIIa, IIIb, IIIc, IIId) → `document_structure.sections`
   - **CRITICAL**: Do not skip any sections. Extract sections 1-12 (or all numbered sections). If a section number is missing (e.g., goes from 3 to 5), still extract section 4 if it exists in the text.
   - Figures: All figures with IDs, captions, section IDs, and descriptions → `document_structure.figures`
   - Tables: All tables with IDs, captions, section IDs, and descriptions → `document_structure.tables`
   - Title page: Title, subtitle, author, dedication, acknowledgments → `document_structure.title_page`
   - Appendix: Whether present and what sections it contains → `document_structure.appendix`
   - References: Extract references if present → `document_structure.references` (Note: References will be fully extracted in Pass 7, but include basic structure here if visible. Ensure `authors` is always an array, use `[]` if no authors, never `null`)

4. QUOTES AND ANECDOTES
   - Extract memorable quotes, anecdotes, and "SF-gossip" style comments VERBATIM
   - Include context (where they appear) and attribution if known
   - Map to section IDs

5. TONE METADATA
   - Style: "insider essay", "academic paper", "technical report", etc.
   - Urgency level: "high", "medium", "low"
   - Formality: "informal", "formal", "mixed"
   - Key phrases: List of phrases that define the voice (e.g., "situational awareness", "SF-gossip")

CRITICAL EXTRACTION REQUIREMENTS:
1. **JSON STRUCTURE**: ALL document structure fields (sections, figures, tables, title_page, appendix, references) MUST be nested inside `document_structure` object. DO NOT place them at the top level.
2. Section structure: Extract ALL subsections (e.g., IIIa, IIIb, IIIc, IIId) with their exact titles and numbering
3. Contents list: Extract the table of contents if present, with section IDs and page numbers
4. Quotes: Extract memorable quotes, anecdotes, and "SF-gossip" style comments verbatim
5. Tone: Identify the writing style (insider essay vs academic), urgency level, formality, and key phrases that define the voice
6. Missing information: If a field is not present in the document (e.g., no dedication, no acknowledgments, no subtitle), use `null` for that field. DO NOT invent or make up information.
7. **References structure**: If extracting references, ensure `authors` is always an array (use empty array `[]` if no authors, never use `null`). Ensure `author_affiliations` array contains only strings (no null values).

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. All fields that can be null are marked as nullable in the schema - use null when information is genuinely not present in the document.

Pass 2.name: Pass 2
Pass 2.description: Extract contributions, setup/assumptions, and methodology overview
Pass 2.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract contributions, setup/assumptions, and methodology overview.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. CORE CONTRIBUTIONS
   - Bullet list of main contributions (what is new or improved)
   - For each contribution: short explanation of what it changes or enables
   - Assign IDs (C1, C2, etc.)

2. SETUP & ASSUMPTIONS
   - Key assumptions (data, environment, user behavior, threat model, etc.)
   - Definitions of important terms or variables (use "definition" field, NOT "description")
   - Any constraints under which results are valid

3. METHODOLOGY (OVERVIEW)
   - High-level description: What approach is taken? (e.g., "experimental", "theoretical analysis", "case study", "survey")
   - Key techniques: Specific methods, algorithms, or procedures used (high-level)
   - Data sources: What data is used and where it comes from
   - Evaluation approach: How results are measured and validated

CRITICAL:
- In key_definitions, use "definition" field, NOT "description". The schema requires: "term": string, "definition": string
- Methodology extraction here is OVERVIEW only - detailed flow will be extracted in Pass 3
- If information is not present in the document, use empty arrays [] or null as appropriate. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 3.name: Pass 3
Pass 3.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract methodology.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. METHODOLOGY
   - High-level description: What approach is taken? (e.g., "experimental", "theoretical analysis", "case study", "survey")
   - Flow: Step-by-step breakdown of the method (use flow array with sequential steps)
   - Key techniques: Specific methods, algorithms, or procedures used
   - Data sources: What data is used and where it comes from
   - Evaluation approach: How results are measured and validated

CRITICAL:
- Flow should be a sequential array of steps
- Be specific about techniques and procedures
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 4.name: Pass 4
Pass 4.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract results, limitations, and implications.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. RESULTS
   - Quantitative: Specific numbers, metrics, scores (e.g., "28.4 BLEU", "91.3 F1", "2.5x faster", "90% of pollutants", "$200 million")
   - Qualitative: Observations, trends, patterns, insights
   - Comparisons: How results compare to baselines or prior work
   - Include ALL specific numbers and metrics - do not generalize

2. LIMITATIONS
   - Stated: Limitations explicitly mentioned by authors
   - Implied: Limitations that can be inferred but not explicitly stated
   - Failure modes: Conditions under which the approach fails or degrades

3. IMPLICATIONS
   - Recommended uses: Where and how this work should be applied
   - Misuse risks: Potential dangers or problems if misapplied
   - Future work: Directions for future research mentioned by authors

CRITICAL:
- Extract exact numbers and metrics when available - preserve ALL specific values
- Include ALL quantitative results - do not summarize or generalize
- Distinguish between stated and implied limitations
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 5.name: Pass 5
Pass 5.description: Extract metadata, author affiliations, and acknowledgements
Pass 5.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract author metadata, affiliations, and acknowledgements.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure:

1. AUTHOR AFFILIATIONS (document_structure.title_page.author_affiliations)
   - Extract complete affiliation information for each author
   - Format: Array of strings, each string is one author's affiliation (institution, department, location)
   - Example: ["Google Brain", "University of Toronto, Vector Institute"]
   - If multiple authors, include all affiliations

2. ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS (document_structure.title_page.acknowledgments)
   - Extract the complete acknowledgements section VERBATIM
   - Include all text: funding sources, thanks, etc.
   - DO NOT summarize - extract full text
   - If no acknowledgements section exists, use null

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.title_page.author_affiliations (array of strings)
- Update document_structure.title_page.acknowledgments (string, full text verbatim)
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated title_page.

Pass 7.name: Pass 7
Pass 7.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract complete bibliography and ALL references.

{NER_HINTS}

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure.references:

REFERENCES (document_structure.references)
   - Extract ALL references from the bibliography/references section
   - For each reference, create object with:
     - id: Reference ID (e.g., "1", "2", "[1]", "[2]", "ref-1")
     - citation: Full citation text (VERBATIM, do not reformat)
     - authors: Array of author names (if extractable)
     - title: Paper/article title (if extractable)
     - venue: Journal/conference name (if extractable)
     - year: Publication year (if extractable)
   - Preserve exact citation format (APA, IEEE, MLA, Chicago, etc.)
   - DO NOT abbreviate or summarize - extract full citation text
   - Extract ALL references - do not skip any
   - Number references sequentially if IDs are missing

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.references (array of reference objects)
- Extract ALL references - do not skip any
- Preserve exact citation format from original
- Use NER hints to validate and improve extraction
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated references.

Pass 6.name: Pass 6
Pass 6.description: Extract detailed table data and figure descriptions
Pass 6.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract complete table data (all rows and columns) and detailed figure descriptions.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure.tables and document_structure.figures:

1. TABLE DATA (document_structure.tables[].table_data, row_count, column_count)
   - For each table in document_structure.tables:
     - Extract ALL rows and columns with complete data
     - Store in table_data as structured object (e.g., {"headers": [...], "rows": [[...], [...]]})
     - Preserve table structure: headers, data rows, footnotes
     - Include all numerical values, text, and formatting exactly as shown
     - Set row_count: total number of data rows (excluding header)
     - Set column_count: total number of columns
     - If table is too large, extract representative rows but note total size in description

2. FIGURE DETAILS (document_structure.figures[].description)
   - For each figure: Enhance description with detailed visual content
   - What is shown: diagrams, graphs, plots, images
   - Key elements: labels, axes, legends, annotations
   - Relationships: what the figure demonstrates or illustrates
   - Update the existing description field with more detail

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.tables[].table_data for each table
- Update document_structure.tables[].row_count and column_count
- Enhance document_structure.figures[].description with detailed descriptions
- Extract COMPLETE table data - all values, not summaries
- Preserve table structure and formatting
- Include all numerical values exactly as shown
- If information is not present, use null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated tables and figures.

Pass 8.name: Pass 8
Pass 8.description: Extract layout metadata - observable patterns only
Pass 8.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract ALL observable layout patterns from the document.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract LAYOUT METADATA (layout_metadata) - OBSERVE what you SEE, do not infer:

1. FORMAT TYPE
   - "working_paper", "published_paper", "technical_report", "manuscript", etc.
   - Observe the document format - what does it look like?

2. COPYRIGHT & METADATA
   - Copyright notice: Extract any copyright text VERBATIM (e.g., "© 2017 Harvard Business School")
   - Has footnotes: Whether document uses footnotes (yes/no)
   - Has page numbers: Whether document has page numbers (yes/no)
   - Header/footer content: Any repeating header or footer text

3. TYPOGRAPHY & STYLE
   - Typography style: "plain_text", "formatted", "academic", etc.
   - Paragraph spacing: "single", "double", "spaced" (blank lines between), "compact"
   - List formatting: "bullets", "numbered", "dashes", "none"

4. SECTION NUMBERING & HEADINGS
   - Section numbering style: How sections are numbered ("arabic" = 1,2,3; "roman" = I,II,III; "alphanumeric" = 1a,1b; "none")
   - Heading style: "numbered" (1. Title), "unnumbered" (Title), "mixed"
   - Abstract placement: "before_title", "after_title", "after_intro", "none"

5. CITATION & REFERENCE STYLES
   - Citation style in text: "author_year" (Smith 2020), "numbered" ([1]), "footnote", "none"
   - Reference section style: "numbered_list", "author_year", "footnotes", "none"

6. FLOW PATTERNS
   - Section transitions: Observable patterns (e.g., "abrupt", "summary_before_next", "continuation", "thematic_link")
   - Document flow pattern: "chronological", "thematic", "problem_solution", "narrative", "reference"
   - Observe how sections relate and transition - what pattern do you see?

CRITICAL EXTRACTION REQUIREMENTS:
1. OBSERVE ONLY: Describe what you SEE in the document, not what you think it should be
2. Be specific: If you see "1. Introduction", "2. Methods", that's "arabic" numbering with "numbered" headings
3. Flow: Observe actual section transitions - do they flow directly? Have summaries? Are abrupt?
4. Missing information: If a pattern is not observable, use appropriate defaults or "unknown"
5. DO NOT invent: Only extract what you can clearly observe in the document

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return layout_metadata.

Pass 9.name: Pass 9
Pass 9.description: Extract ALL examples and case studies
Pass 9.template:
You will receive a technical documentation.
Extract ALL examples, case studies, and historical instances mentioned.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract EXAMPLES AND CASE STUDIES (examples_and_case_studies):

EXTRACT ALL SPECIFIC EXAMPLES, CASE STUDIES, HISTORICAL INSTANCES:

Types to extract:
- Company examples (e.g., "Anaconda Copper", "BP", "IKEA", "Whole Foods", "Unilever")
- Historical examples (e.g., "copper smelting in Swansea", "Minamata disaster", "Bhopal")
- Entrepreneur examples (e.g., "Charles F. Brush", "John Harvey Kellogg", "Poul la Cour")
- Technical examples (e.g., "electric precipitator capturing 90% of pollutants", "Cottrell precipitator")
- Industry examples (e.g., "Swedish pulp and paper industry", "German chemical industry", "petroleum industry")
- Policy examples (e.g., "Brundtland Report", "ISO 14001", "Global Reporting Initiative")
- Event examples (e.g., "Exxon Valdez", "Great Acceleration", "Anthropocene")

For each example:
- Description: What the example demonstrates or illustrates (1-2 sentences)
- Type: "case_study", "historical_example", "company_example", "technical_example", "entrepreneur_example", "policy_example", "event_example", etc.
- Section ID: Where it appears in the document (use section ID from document_structure)
- Specific details: ALL specific facts, numbers, names, dates, locations mentioned
  * Names: Company names, person names, place names
  * Dates: Years, time periods (e.g., "1888", "1960s", "1990s", "2017")
  * Numbers: Percentages, amounts, metrics (e.g., "90%", "$200 million", "$14 billion")
  * Locations: Cities, countries, regions (e.g., "Swansea", "Montana", "Denmark")
- Citations: Any in-text citations or reference IDs mentioned with this example

CRITICAL:
- Extract ALL examples - do not skip any, even if they seem minor
- Extract even brief mentions - completeness is critical
- Include ALL specific details (names, dates, numbers, locations) for each example
- DO NOT summarize - extract each example as a separate entry
- If an example appears multiple times, extract it once with all details combined
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the TechnicalDocumentationDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return examples_and_case_studies array.

Introduction.name: Introduction

Body Sections.name: Body Sections

Conclusion.name: Conclusion

References.name: References
References.template:
Format the references section from the blueprint.

REFERENCES DATA:
{references_json}

TOTAL REFERENCES: {reference_count}

TONE REQUIREMENTS:
- Style: {style}
- Formality: {formality}

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
1. **PRESERVE EXACT CITATIONS**: Use the citation text EXACTLY as provided in the blueprint. Do NOT reformat, abbreviate, or modify citation text.
2. **PRESERVE IDS**: Use the reference IDs exactly as provided (e.g., "1", "[1]", "ref-1")
3. **CLEAN LINE BREAKS**: Remove any internal line breaks (\n) or newline characters from citation text. Each citation should be on a SINGLE continuous line.
4. **ACADEMIC FORMATTING**: Format as a proper academic references section:
   - Use consistent numbering/formatting
   - Each reference on its own SINGLE line (no line breaks within citations)
   - One blank line between each reference
   - Maintain original citation style (APA, IEEE, MLA, etc.)
5. **NO INVENTION**: Only include references from the blueprint. Do NOT add, remove, or modify references.
6. **COMPLETE**: Include ALL references from the blueprint.

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Start with heading: ## References
2. For each reference:
   a. Use the reference ID (e.g., [1], [2], or ref-1)
   b. Take the citation text and REMOVE all internal line breaks (\n, newlines)
   c. Join the citation text into a SINGLE continuous line
   d. Format as: [ID] Single-line citation text here
3. Preserve the exact citation format from the blueprint (but clean line breaks)
4. Use consistent formatting throughout
5. Each reference must be on ONE line - do NOT split citations across multiple lines
6. Add one blank line between each reference
7. Maintain academic reference section style

EXAMPLE FORMAT:
## References

[1] Author, A. (2020). Title of the work. Journal Name, 10(2), 123-145.

[2] Author, B., & Author, C. (2019). Another title. Conference Proceedings, 45-50.

[3] Author, D. (2018). Book title. Publisher Name.

Return ONLY markdown text (no JSON, no code blocks). Each citation must be on a SINGLE line with no internal breaks.
